skill_title: Compare two datasets using central tendency and spread
notes: 20-item bank. CAPS mix: 10 L3 / 10 L4. Compare two groups using mean/median + IQR/range. Make justified statements.

stimulus.inline: Boys mean 65, girls mean 72 on a test.
Boys range 35-95 (range 60); girls range 60-85 (range 25).
Two classes' mean Maths Lit marks: 68 vs 75.
Class A: median 60, IQR 30. Class B: median 60, IQR 12.

items.question: Centres equal; which is more CONSISTENT?

stimulus.inline: Compare incomes: Region A mean R12 000, median R10 000; Region B mean R10 500, median R10 000. Same median.

items.question: What does A's higher mean suggest?
options: A has some very high outlier earners pulling the mean up
items.expectedAnswer: A has some very high outlier earners pulling the mean up
workingSteps: Higher mean with equal median → right-skew/outliers in A.

stimulus.inline: Sports times (lower = faster). Athletes A: median 12s, IQR 1,5. Athletes B: median 11,8, IQR 3.
Same. More consistent?
Two schools' matric pass rates: School X 75%, School Y 82%.
Class C average 65 ± 10 (std dev illustrative). Class D 70 ± 20.
Two heights samples: Boys avg 175 cm, Girls avg 162 cm. Same range 50 cm.

items.question: Statement?
options: Boys taller on average, similar variability
items.expectedAnswer: Boys taller on average, similar variability
workingSteps: Boys mean higher; same range → similar spread.

stimulus.inline: **Two box plots**: Class A min 30, Q1 55, med 65, Q3 75, max 85. Class B min 40, Q1 60, med 70, Q3 80, max 90.

items.question: Class B's median is HIGHER by:

stimulus.inline: Same box plots. IQRs?
Same. Ranges?

items.question: Which has SMALLER range?
workingSteps: A: 85-30=55. B: 90-40=50. Actually B smaller by 5. Correction: B has smaller range.

stimulus.inline: Compare TV-time means. Class X: 2,5 h/day. Class Y: 4 h/day.
Group A 30 learners mean 65. Group B 50 learners mean 70. Combined mean?
Justify a statement. School X pass rate 75% with n=200; School Y 82% with n=20.

items.question: Most defensible claim?
options: Y has higher rate but small sample size makes the comparison less reliable
X outperforms Y because larger n
items.expectedAnswer: Y has higher rate but small sample size makes the comparison less reliable

stimulus.inline: Mean income: Region A R8 000, B R10 000. Median: A R7 500, B R8 000.

items.question: Which has more INEQUALITY (skewed)?
workingSteps: B's mean (10 000) is much higher than median (8 000) — more right-skew (outliers).

stimulus.inline: Daily commute times. Bus mean 45 min ± 10 min; Train mean 35 min ± 5 min.
Class A 25 learners avg 70. Class B 25 learners avg 80. Combined mean?
Class A 40 learners avg 60; Class B 10 learners avg 90. Combined?

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_MEAN_COMPARE: Picks the lower of two means as 'higher' or vice versa.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_AVERAGE_CHOICE: Picks wrong average for skewed data.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_WEIGHTED_MEAN: Mean of two groups computed as simple avg when n differs.
